chapter: Des Moines childhood and first bands
title: Edgar Pillows and his Night Owls
summary: A hod carrier named Edgar Pillows asked about the orchestration Barefield was carrying, joined the band on tuba and became its leader. The group, with an older banjoist and later a tap-dancing drummer, played homecomings around Iowa.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Around 1925, I was downtown one day and they were building the Capital Theater on Grand Avenue. I had gone to the music store and bought an orchestration on "Aggravating Papa," I think it was. And as I was going home there was a hod carrier who came over to me you know, put his stick there and said, hey, son, what's that you've got? Music? I said, "yes." He said, "well, let me see it." I showed it to him and he said, "well, could I have a second trumpet part, do you have it? I said, "yes," because we didn't have but one trumpet. He said, "what are you going to do with this music?" I said, "well, we've got a little band and we're going to play." he said, "May I come and hear your band?" Yes.

His name was Edgar Pillows (PHONETIC) and he was an older man. He came up one day and he heard us rehearse. He got himself an E flat tuba and started rehearsing with us. He finally took us over and called us Edgar Pillows' Night Owls. It was just the five of us. No, we had one more man, older man, which was a banjo player, Emery Henry Green. So it was Edgar Pillows who was the leader, Emery Henry Green the banjo player and --
Piano and drums. We really started playing for homecomings around and playing all over the state, different places.

Oh, Edgar -- we were kids, say the oldest of us was about 16 and he was in his 20's, you know. Emery and Edgar Henry Green was in his 30's or maybe near 40, he was a much older guy. But then Melvin Saunders the little fellow, the drummer, he was so young that we had to leave him off and we got an older drummer named Carl Shelton. He was a tap dancer and a drummer.
